title: Picking a clip, clicking a cut and keying or undoing a value answer inside 50 ms
goal: On a video, a first click on a clip, a click on a cut, the first value picked to animate in a session, and Undo of that key each still keep the app busy for a little over 50 ms (about 53 to 63 ms), against the 50 ms the video goals ask for. Both measurements point at the same cost: the whole window laying itself out and the Mac's accessibility bookkeeping walking every view. Bring all four under 50 ms, and make the loop's test copy report what a person actually gets.
notes:
Carried from picking-a-cut-or-a-first-clip-on-the-timeline-an (2026-10-07), whose log has every number. Shipped there: markers hang only in a probe launched with --playtest (AppFlavor.hangsWalkMarkers, PlaytestMarkers.areHung), so the dev app sheds ~800 marker views. Markerless stand-in (all markers off but the walk's timeline ones): first pick 48-60 (median ~56), cut 47-60 (~53). Probe with markers: first 78-86, cut 73-81. Levers measured, none shipped: (a) probe marker teardown deferred 0.3 s (retain the marker view and its AppKitPlatformViewHost in a static dismantleNSView) cut 75 -> 67; (b) CollapsibleSection header as an EquatableView keyed on title/chip, -2..3 ms; needs the onReorder/onReorderEnd closures to read the live section list (reveal.drawnSections) and the accessory (EditPoint/Transition header notes) in its key. (c) The big remaining cost of a first pick is SwiftUI's accessibility focus walk: AccessibilityNode.updateFocusResponder ~50 times per pick (lldb breakpoint count), each visiting every responder (ViewRendererHost.focusResponder, swift_conformsToProtocol); fewer AppKit-backed views in the window shrinks every run. An out-of-process accessibility client is live on this Mac, so it is real for users. Marker redesign idea for (2): markers that are not SwiftUI platform views (a few per-scroll-view hosts holding plain NSView markers positioned from onGeometryChange) keep the harness's NSView reads but take ~800 views out of SwiftUI's bookkeeping; the harness reads frames, visibleRect, enclosing scroll views and isHiddenOrHasHiddenAncestor off them (PlaytestPanelPress.fieldViews/scrollAreas), so every nested ScrollView needs its own host. Profiling recipe: xcrun xctrace record --template 'Time Profiler' --attach <probe pid> during the walk; a walk of only first picks or only cuts makes every heavy window one of them.

Folded in from undoing-a-key-and-the-first-key-of-a-session-ans (daily digest 2026-10-07, same root cause):
Carried from keying-a-value-redraws-only-what-the-key-changes (2026-10-07), whose log has every number. Shipped there: Text, Appearance, Effects, Time and Captions watch EditorState.lookRowsRevision (moves for anything but a key on position/scale/rotation/crop, PhotonzDocument.sameApartFromPlacementKeys) through readingForTheLookRows, so a Position pick builds none of them (expectBuilds in keyframe-anything-walk); perform/undo/redo/discardDragPreview no longer write unchanged previews or selection. Result: stopwatch pick 46-47 -> 44, first pick in keyframe-anything 57-59 -> 53-55, an-editing-session 59-65 (unchanged), undo 63-68 (unchanged within noise).

What is left is not view bodies (<10% of the pass by Time Profiler: xctrace record --attach <probe pid> --template 'Time Profiler', export the time-profile table, group main-thread samples by burst). It is AttributeGraph propagation (ObservationGraphMutation.apply, Subgraph::update), layout of the whole window, and SwiftUI's accessibility focus walk, the same root cause a-first-clip-pick-and-a-cut-click-answer-inside names. Ruled out by measurement: walk markers (all but four off: pick 47, undo 61, no change), the canvas refit when the timeline grows (deferred a pass: no change), Effects/Text/Appearance/Time bodies (now skipped: ~2 ms), restoreSelectionFromHistory/publishSharedComponents/TutorialController on undo (switched off: no change). Measured but not shipped: the timeline keeping its height when a key lane opens (it grows 25pt, the dock shrinks and the picture refits 74% -> 71%): pick -7 ms, keyframe-anything first pick 48-49, an-editing-session 52-54, undo still ~55; that is a visible behaviour change and would need a decision card. Undo and a pick take the same ~85-90 ms from the change to the main thread next sleeping (CFRunLoop beforeWaiting observer); the walk's 'longest pass' is lower for a pick only because that work is cut into more passes. First-pick extra (~10 ms over later picks) shows as Swift metadata/conformance lookups on first use of the row and lane views.
acceptance: On clip-click-cost-walk, a cut click and a first clip pick each hold the main thread under 50 ms in nine of ten clicks over three runs, none over 100 ms
The number the walk reports is within a few ms of what the same clicks cost without the walk's markers (they are about 20-25 ms today), or the walk says how much of its number is its own markers
The panel still shows the cut (Edit point, Transition) after a cut click and the clip after a piece click, in the click's own frame
The first value picked from Animate a property in a session (Position on a typed title) holds the main thread under 50 ms in three runs each of keyframe-anything-walk and an-editing-session-walk
Undoing that pick holds under 50 ms in Scripts/playtest/perf/animate-pick-cost-walk.json (median of twelve)
keyframe-anything-walk keeps its body-count claims: a Position key builds Properties and none of Text, Appearance, Effects or Time

log.note: daily digest 2026-10-07: merged undoing-a-key-and-the-first-key-of-a-session-ans into this task. Both runners traced the rest of the cost to the same place (AttributeGraph propagation, whole-window layout, SwiftUI's accessibility focus walk), so one runner attacking that cause should measure all four presses. Its acceptance items and notes are now here; title and goal widened to match.

Measured 2026-10-07 07:00-08:00. Probe with markers: first pick 80-84, cut 76-84. Built setup timedWithoutMarkers (markers taken down around each timed press/action, walk notes what the teardown cost): first pick 33-48, cut 46-72, deselect 40-62 depending on machine load. Profile with markers: 18% of the heavy pass is SwiftUI's accessibility focus walk, half of it over the markers' platform views; without markers the focus walk mostly goes. Tried and reverted: sections leaving a pass later (kept built, drawn as nothing): interleaved A/B/C showed it SLOWER for cuts (64-72 vs 46-60) because moving/hiding eight built sections costs as much as tearing them down. Noise between rounds is 15-20ms (an xctrace SwiftUI recording in the background); only interleaved runs compare.

No audit: nothing a person sees changed; this is the walks' stopwatch. Left rough, folded into the carried task's notes: tutorial anchors hang in every build even with no guide running (-2 to -3 ms a cut if hung only while one runs); a dropdown's face is a nested NSHostingView (~2 ms of a cut's teardown for nine).
